E0102	malformed number %q		
E0103	unknown escape %s in string		
E0104	unterminated string		
E0105	malformed duration %q		
E0106	`\u{%s}` is not a Unicode scalar value		`\u{…}` takes a code point up to 10FFFF that is not a surrogate (D800–DFFF); for a byte, write `\xHH`
E0110	unexpected %s		
E0111	comparison operators cannot be chained		split it with `and`: a < b and b < c
E0112	expected %s, found %s		
E0113	duplicate key `%s` in a map literal or pattern		
E0114	test must be at the top level		
E0115	expression nesting too deep (limit %d)		
E0116	argument `%s` given twice		
E0117	`%s()` has no arguments		a tag without arguments is a symbol: write it without the parentheses
E0118	a range cannot be an operand of another range		`..` does not chain: put the inner range in parentheses if you mean it
E0119	parameter `%s` is bound twice		
E0120	a required parameter cannot follow an optional one		move the parameters with a default to the end, or give this one a default too
E0121	a tag takes its values by position, not by name		write `Tag(a, b)`; for named fields put a map in it: `Tag({a: 1})`
E0122	a string with `${…}` cannot be %s		only a constant string fits here: drop the interpolation
E0123	`_` cannot be a named argument		`_` fills a position; for a named one write a lambda: `x => f(a: x)`
E0124	an anonymous function cannot be written with `=`		anonymous functions take a block: `fn(x): … ;;`, or write a lambda `x => …`
E0125	`%s` binds looser than `..`, so it cannot be an end of a slice		put the end in parentheses: `xs[(a or b)..]`
E0126	a positional argument cannot follow a named one		put the positional arguments first: `f(1, b: 2)`
E0127	`??` and `|>` cannot be mixed without parentheses		say which one goes first: `(x |> f) ?? d` or `x |> (f ?? d)`
E0128	a symbol is not written with an uppercase letter: `'%s`		an uppercase symbol is written as the tag, without the quote: `Red`
E0129	`$%s` in a string is not interpolation		write `${name}` for the value, or `\$name` for the text
E0130	a type annotation has no element type		write `list` or `map` alone: the elements are not checked, so they are not written
E0131	this statement comes after `return`, so it never runs	never runs	remove it, or move the `return` after it
E0132	`return` used as a value		`return` stands as a statement or ends a branch (`if`, `match`, `then … else`); compute the value first, then return it
E0133	a spread `...` cannot stand %s		`...xs` spreads a list or a range into a call's last positional argument: `f(a, ...xs, k: v)`; to join lists, use `+`
E0134	`%s` is not a keyword in fung		
E0135	number %q is out of range		
E0136	a statement after another cannot begin its line with `-`		to continue the line before, end that line with the `-`; a negative value on a line of its own is written in parentheses: `(-x)`
E0204	undefined name `%s`	not found in this scope	
E0205	cannot assign to `%s` here: it is bound outside this block		a name is bound once, and a block cannot bind an outer one again; build the value with an expression instead, e.g. `x = if … ;;` or `fold`
E0206	`%s` is not visible here: it was defined inside a block		assign the block's value instead: `x = if … ;;`
E0208	local function `%s` is defined later in this block		local functions can only call themselves; move both functions to the top level
E0209	cannot reassign `%s`: it is a function or an imported name		
E0210	function `%s` is defined twice		
E0211	%s %s		use `exit()` to stop a script early
E0212	unknown type `%s`		
E0213	return inside a for body		not used: merged into E0237
E0214	`?` outside a function		use `!` to stop the script on Err
E0215	`_` can only be a call argument or a pattern		
E0216	alternatives of a pattern must bind the same names		
E0217	type `%s` is defined twice		
E0218	type `%s` refers to itself		
E0219	type aliases must be at the top level		
E0220	`?` inside a for body		not used: merged into E0237
E0221	name `%s` is bound twice in one pattern		use a guard to compare the two positions: `[a, b] when a == b`
E0222	`%s` is a built-in type and cannot be a type alias		give the alias another name
E0223	`if` without `else` used as a value: it is nil when the condition is false	this if has no else	add an `else:` branch; write `else: nil` if nil is meant (a function that returns nothing ends in `else: nil` or `nil`)
E0224	a block used as a value %s, so the value is nil		end the block with the value it stands for, e.g. the assigned name on its own line; write `nil` last if nil is meant
E0225	`%s` starts with an uppercase letter, so it is a tag and cannot name a variable	this is a tag	name variables in lowercase: `{HOME: home} = cfg`, `max_retries = 3`
E0226	`?` inside a lambda given to %s		not used: merged into E0237
E0227	`_` in a call on the right of `|>`		the piped value is always the first argument; to put it elsewhere, call a parenthesised partial: `x |> (f(1, _))` (or a lambda: `x |> (v => f(1, v))`)
E0228	the rest parameter `...%s` is always a list		annotate it `list`, or not at all
E0229	`%s` on the right of `|>` applies to the call, not to the pipe		put the pipe in parentheses: `(xs |> try_map(f))?`
E0230	too many %s (limit %d)		
E0231	a block used as a value %s, so the value is nil		not used: merged into E0224
E0232	`%s` takes no element type		not used: element types are gone, see E0130
E0233	the test name %q %s		give each test in a file its own name: the report names a failed test by it
E0234	%s is computed and discarded		use the value, or write `_ = …` to discard it on purpose
E0235	this arm %s		move it last, or give it a guard: `n when n > 0 =>`
E0236	`%s` takes exactly one value, found %d		put several values in a tuple: `Ok((a, b))` or `Err((a, b))`
E0237	`%s` inside %s		a lambda `=>` and a `for` body cannot return early; write an anonymous `fn(x): … ;;` to return from, or use `try_map`, `find`, `all`/`any` or `fold`
E0238	cannot bind `%s` again: a name is bound once		give the new value a name of its own, or compute it in one expression (a pipe, `x = if … ;;`, `fold`)
E0239	unused %s `%s`		remove it, or start its name with `_` if it is kept on purpose
E0240	`%s` hides %s		a visible name means one thing: give the new one a name of its own
E0241	this alternative never matches: %s		remove it
E0242	the test %q checks nothing: its body is empty		give it an `assert`, or remove it
E0243	`??` after %s: it is never nil or a result, so the right side is never used		remove the `??`, or put it after the value that can be missing
E0301	cannot find module `%s`		standard library modules are imported by name (`import fs`); your own files by path (`import "./lib/x"`)

E0518	%s is not valid UTF-8: %s		a string can hold any bytes, but this needs text; check where the bytes came from, or test them with `is_utf8(s)`
E0519	%s in %s: it is not put into text silently		unwrap a result with `!` or `?` and give `nil` a default with `??` first; to show any value as `print` does, write `str(x)`
E0520	file `%s` is not open for %s		open it with the mode the code needs: `fs.open(p, 'read)` to read, `'write` or `'append` to write
E0521	the replacement names group `%s`, which the pattern does not have		name a group the pattern has: `$1`, `${name}`; write `${1}a` for group 1 then `a` (`$1a` is the name `1a`), and `$$` for a `$`
E0522	range start %d is after its end %d		the empty ranges are `n..n` and `n..=n-1`; if the end may fall below the start, say so: `a..max(a, b)`
E0523	the int %d has no exact float value		a float holds every int up to 2^53 exactly; to round on purpose, write `float(n)`
E0524	`%d ** %d`: an int to a negative int power is not an int		write the exponent as a float: `2 ** -1.0`
